prompt: Which statement defines kinetic energy in Cambridge International AS Level Physics?
options: energy that an object has because of its motion
the work done to raise an object through a vertical distance
the product of the resultant force on an object and its velocity
the rate at which momentum is transferred during motion

answer.explanation: Kinetic energy is defined as the energy that an object has because of its motion.

distractor_explanations: Option 1 is correct. This is the exact controlled syllabus definition: energy that an object has because of its motion.
Option 2 defines gravitational potential energy, not kinetic energy.
Option 3 defines mechanical power (P = Fv), not kinetic energy.
Option 4 defines resultant force according to Newton's second law (F = dp/dt), not kinetic energy.
hints: Recall the controlled definition of kinetic energy from the syllabus.
Focus on the concise definition regarding energy possessed due to motion.
solution: Kinetic energy is defined as the energy that an object has because of its motion. Option 1 is correct.
teacher_walkthrough: State the exact syllabus definition: energy that an object has because of its motion.
Distinguish kinetic energy (scalar, measured in joules) from momentum (vector) and power (rate).
